title: Al 3+ -substituted Co–Zn nanoferrites as magnetically separable adsorbents for trypan blue: composition effect, isotherm, kinetic and thermodynamic analysis
content: Spinel ferrites can be recovered from water magnetically, but the effect of Al3+ substitution on their uptake of anionic azo dyes is unclear. Co0.6−xZn0.4−xAl2xFe2O4 nanoferrites (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.08) were synthesized by co-precipitation and evaluated for the first time as adsorbents for trypan blue (TB), a sulfonated azo dye classed as possibly carcinogenic. XRD confirmed a cubic spinel structure (Fd3̄m) with a minor α-Fe2O3 phase (<0.4%); crystallite size decreased from 16.3 to 12.4 nm, and the lattice parameter increased from 8.3667 to 8.3801 Å with Al3+ content. At pH 2 and 0.4 g L−1, TB removal rose from 47.5% (x = 0) to 86.6% (x = 0.06), although the geometric surface area increased by only about 32%, so surface area alone does not explain the gain. Dye-only and adsorbent-blank controls confirmed that the removal was due to adsorption. For x = 0.06 at 25 °C, uptake approached pseudo-equilibrium within 140 min; removal was 98.2% at 5.15 mg L−1 and 72.8% at 27.56 mg L−1, with an observed capacity of 50.14 mg g−1 at 0.4 g L−1 (Langmuir estimate 55.8 ± 7.5 mg g−1; the Freundlich model fitted slightly better). Kinetics followed a pseudo-second-order model. Apparent thermodynamic parameters indicated a spontaneous, exothermic, predominantly physical process (ΔH° = −40.9 kJ mol−1). About 93% of the removal efficiency remained after five regeneration cycles. Metal release at pH 2 was limited (fifth cycle: 0.88 mg L−1 Co, 2.2 mg L−1 Fe) but may exceed discharge limits. The adsorbent is easily separated magnetically, but its moderate capacity, acidic optimum pH, and metal release limit practical use.
